page-organizations-public-sector-case-st: Bhutan has anchored its National Digital Identity system on Ethereum, enabling citizens to control verifiable credentials without relying exclusively on a central identity database.
Governments and international organizations are already using Ethereum-based infrastructure for identity, records, finance, and humanitarian programs.

Giga, a joint initiative of UNICEF and ITU, worked with the Government of Rwanda to test whether Ethereum staking rewards could provide a recurring source of financing for school connectivity. The rewards paid about $5,600 in school internet fees.
Giga: School connectivity funded by staking

The International Training Centre of the ILO issues digital certificates and badges that can be independently verified using Ethereum. Learners share them with employers and institutions without a crypto wallet or any knowledge of Ethereum. More than 208,000 had been issued by October 2025.
UNICEF's CryptoFund uses Ethereum and Ethereum-based assets to receive, hold, and distribute funds while improving auditability and keeping beneficiary data offchain.

page-organizations-public-sector-fits-de: Ethereum can complement existing government databases or services. It is most useful where multiple parties need to coordinate without giving one participant exclusive control of the shared record.

page-organizations-public-sector-hero-de: Open digital infrastructure for public services, identity, funding, and trusted records.

Ethereum gives governments and public-interest organizations a shared infrastructure that is globally accessible, independently verifiable, and not controlled by a single company or state. Sensitive information can remain private while Ethereum provides settlement, verification, or auditability.
page-organizations-public-sector-meta-de: How governments and NGOs use Ethereum as open digital public infrastructure for verifiable credentials, public records and transparent funding.
page-organizations-public-sector-use-cas: Explore how Ethereum can support public services while strengthening transparency, interoperability, and sovereignty for countries, institutions, and individuals.
Issue bonds, move digital money, or coordinate settlement using shared infrastructure while retaining existing legal and regulatory frameworks.
Distribute funds digitally while making flows easier to verify and audit, without publishing sensitive beneficiary information.
Give people verifiable credentials they can control and reuse across services without depending on a single centralized identity database.
Issue property titles, licenses, and diplomas that anyone can check are genuine. A university can issue a digital diploma that an employer verifies without seeing the graduate's other personal data.
